questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have always wanted to come to the Bay Area to experience the pulsing start-up scene and better understand why this area in particular is so good at it.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Really easy UC Berkeley treated UCEAP students much better than other international students from universities without an exchange agreement.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We where part of the orientation together with students transferring from other colleges and thus got the all needed information. If I could give some feedback it would be to taylor it slightly more to internationals as we got a bit to much irrelevant information.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of options to live "on-campus" (on-campus in Berkeley is the term used when living in close proximity to the campus as no students are living on campus except those sleeping in the libraries). I lived in the International House which is an independent organisation affiliated with the university, I was also offered housing through the university however I choose not to live there as it is mostly freshmen living there, i.e. very young americans. The last option I know off outside of finding something private is the CO-OPs which is the most affordable housing option.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: At the international house all residents are on a meal plan and all meals are prepared for you.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The Bay Area is expensive, expect slightly worn down houses, shared rooms, and food of a lower quality than Denmark

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Registration at UC Berkeley was very easy. I recommend doing it ASAP as you will need the papers for your visa application, which is a longer process

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: If in doubt you can write the Berkeley International Office

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very – UCEAP students get to register at the same time as transfer students (around 2 months before) and most of the courses I considered was not filled at that point. Additionally there is a add-and-drop period the first month where people change courses

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: One can sign up to at most 20 units at UC Berkeley, this is equivalent to around ~ 50 ECTS (I needed just 12 UC Berkeley units to get my 30 ETCS). I recommend using all of those 20 units and then drop courses later as some will get filled.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
I took 1 graduate level course, ECON 230B Public Economics. It was the continuation of 230A which I had not taken but felt like I could still follow the course without any problems and the level was on par with a master's course at UCPH. I also took 3 upper-division undergrad courses (as a undergrad UCEAP student you are allow to take just 1 grad-course) though upper-division I would say the level is below what I had in the final year of my bachelor's degree. 
I believe the reason for this is the fact that people can choose courses much more freely than at UCPH and thus they have to start at a lower level to ensure people without a background in e.g. economics can follow an upper-division econ course.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style itself is similar to that of UCPH, however the grading is not done anonymously as at UCPH. In some courses showing up to class is counted towards the grade and even in the case where it is not as grading is not done anonymously having some sort of relationship with the professor could help sway your grade. This I am personally not a fan of but just part of the system unfortunately.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: ECON 230B Public Economics, ECON 148 Data Science for Economists, ECON 136 Financial Economics, UGBA 128 Strategic Cost Management

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
ECON 230B is a great course for all economics masters students I would say and further it is currently taught by Emanuel Saez. 
ECON 148 is a great Data Science course with a focus on applications to economists but easily generalized to other social sciences and only basic economics is needed to understand the course. As DATA (their data science major) is quiet popular it might be easier to get ECON 148 than a DATA course.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: To be honest not really that many unexpected costs I had foreseen most. The only thing is just that California, and the Bay in particular is crazy expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: All prices are similar to what you would pay in Denmark except clothing where you can get some good deals.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are casual sports clubs e.g., running, hiking, dancing, etc. However, as UC Berkeley is a university with, lets be honest, many over achievers a lot of the clubs are centered around something more serious. I counted at least 10 different investment clubs and 20+ consulting clubs – I personally did not participate in this as I was not here for that reason.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go watch basket games and if in here during fall also football games, it is an experience especially when facing the UC Berkeley rivals from Standford.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: San Francisco is obvious but for something more go to the national parks e.g. Yosemite or Sequoia or take a plane somewhere. It is relatively cheap to fly to San Diego/Los Angeles/Las Vegas etc.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It is difficult, I only have a few people I would consider friends from the US, most are very young.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Very specific to the Bay Area, but the entrepreneurial spirit was nice to experience

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Time is limited, make the most of it while you can. It is not as difficult as one might believe (some classes I considered easy for most last year bachelor's student or a master's student as long as they are within your field). Seize the day, just by talking to people I have ended up at networking events at investment banks and A.I. conferences in Palo Alto.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Friendships

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Balancing traveling and studies

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
